correctness.rationale: In every fixed-sum four-part partition, specifying three canonical occurrence labels forces the fourth value, giving at most one completion. If a nontrivial 2-intersecting family has a pair meeting in exactly two labels, split it into members containing their common pair (at most 4 using a family member missing that pair), containing exactly one (at most 8 by choosing one label from each disjoint residual pair), or containing none (at most 1). If all pairs meet in >=3 labels, fixing one member bounds family size by 4. Thus nontrivial families have size <=13. The maximum 2-star has floor((n-2)/2) members, >13 for \(n\ge30\). Two distinct exact finite methods establish all 26 remaining \(4\le n\le29\) maxima: bitset maximum clique with proved coloring bound, and independently implemented full Bron--Kerbosch maximal-clique enumeration with separate ambient generator. Direct subset brute force agrees for \(n\le13\). The only strict exception is \(n=9\) with four explicit mutually 2-intersecting partitions. Both programs were executed from their actual embedded file paths and full outputs examined.

originality.rationale: The theorem fixes \(k=4,t=2\) for all n and is an exact natural classification absent from the examined same-object primary sources. Borg Conjecture 1.6 and Remark 1.5 explicitly own the known order-nine exception and Lemma 3.1 owns the auxiliary nontrivial-family bound; they do not imply the twenty-two or so unresolved finite intermediate values. Person--Schweser Theorem 1.1 requires sufficiently large k and Theorem 1.2 studies distinct large-k counterexamples; neither specializes to fixed four-part all-order bounds. Full primary material and semantic equivalences compared; possibility of unindexed exact work remains.
residual_risks: No literature search rules out unindexed or not-yet-published equivalent fixed-(4,2) classifications.

The bounded extremal values use executable finite enumeration, not a short closed-form hand proof for each of the 26 intermediate orders; two independently implemented exact enumeration algorithms and an auxiliary exhaustive subset check limit computational risk.

Its value is the complete natural statement, not the earlier-known exception or the previously implied cap by themselves.
